digest.top_line: HDR mould/flap skin brachy for BCC/cSCC: 5yr actuarial LC 98% (n=136), 2yr LC 84.9%, no G3+ late toxicity across four single-institution series.
digest.tldr: Skin was the day's only site. HDR surface mould and catheter-flap series report LC 84.9-98% with no G3+ late toxicity, but all four are single-institution cohorts with no comparator vs surgery or EBRT. Short follow-up in the modern series (median 8 and 15 mo) limits the late-toxicity read.

sites.intro: Dose and fractionation for HDR skin brachy vary widely (30 Gy/5 fx to 64 Gy/32 fx), and pretibial skin carries most of the reported severe toxicity.

studies.name: HDR skin brachytherapy: surface mould and flap series
studies.tldr: Mould/flap HDR for BCC/cSCC: 5yr actuarial LC 98% (n=136), 1yr LC 92% (flap), 2yr LC 84.9%; no G3+ late toxicity reported in any series.

studies.significance: Depth, not fractionation, is the gating parameter: series using 180 cGy daily, 40 Gy/10 fx and 40 Gy/8 fx twice weekly all report LC in the 85-98% band when prescribed at 5 mm, while survey respondents avoid brachy beyond 3 mm depth. Pretibial skin is the one site where respondents converge on gentler 2-3 Gy fractions.
studies.monday_clinic: In elderly or surgery-averse pts with superficial facial or pinna BCC/cSCC on curved surfaces, these series support mould or flap HDR as an RT option; they do not extend to lesions deeper than about 5 mm, perineural invasion, or pretibial skin.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Four single-institution series (Guix prospective, n=136; Allan, n=13; Casey retrospective, 59 pts; Gogineni retrospective, 50 pts) plus a **30-question ABS survey with 16 respondents**.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Ir-192 HDR via custom PMMA moulds, Aquaplast/supraflab moulds or a silicone catheter flap with channels **5 mm from the surface and 10 mm apart**. Regimens span **6000-6500 cGy at 180 cGy/fx**, **45 Gy/8 fx over 5 days**, **40 Gy/10 fx** and **40 Gy/8 fx twice weekly**.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: No series reported G3+ late toxicity; Gogineni had **acute G3 in 5%** and Casey **one G2 necrosis**. Survey respondents flagged **severe toxicity on pretibial skin**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Guix benchmarks against Lovett's EBRT series (superficial X-ray LC 95%, electrons 77%). Gogineni cites the sole surgery vs RT randomised trial in facial BCC, where 4-year failure was **7.5% vs 0.7%** favoring surgery.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents superficial BCC/cSCC of the face, scalp and pinna in pts unsuitable for or declining surgery. Does not represent deep (beyond ~5 mm), perineural, previously irradiated, or pretibial lesions.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Similar control across very different dose-per-fraction schedules suggests depth selection and dosimetric coverage drive outcome more than schedule. **No consensus on dosimetric constraints** exists per the survey, so plan quality is operator-dependent.

studies.interpretation:
Taken together, these papers make a consistent argument that surface mould and flap HDR brachytherapy controls superficial basal and squamous cell carcinoma of the face and ear at rates comparable to other radiation techniques, with little late toxicity. The consistency is real but it is the consistency of selected institutional experience. Every outcome cohort here is single-arm, histology is mixed or pooled, and the two modern series report median follow-up of 8 and 15 months, which is short for a disease whose local failures in the Guix cohort appeared at 17 to 23 months. The only randomised evidence cited across the set, the facial BCC trial referenced by Gogineni, favored surgery on 4-year failure (7.5% vs 0.7%), and none of these series addresses that gap directly.

The more useful signal is what stays constant across very different schedules. Guix delivered 180 cGy daily to 6000-6500 cGy over roughly seven weeks; Casey most often used 40 Gy in 10 fractions; Gogineni gave 40 Gy in 8 fractions twice weekly; Allan used 45 Gy in 8 fractions over five days on the pinna. Reported control sits in a similar band across all of them, and toxicity is low across all of them. What is shared is the geometry: prescription at or near 5 mm, margins near 5 mm, and applicators built to hold source-to-skin distance constant over curved surfaces. That points to depth selection and coverage, rather than the fractionation choice, as the variable a radiation oncologist should be most careful about. The survey reinforces this from practice: respondents avoid brachytherapy for depth over 3 mm, perineural invasion and prior RT, and sixty percent estimate depth by ultrasound before treating.

The population boundaries matter. Guix's 87% control in recurrent tumors versus 99% in primaries, and Allan's insistence on sparing uninvolved cartilage, both argue that the technique performs best on untreated, thin lesions. Casey's cohort is older (median 82) and includes melanoma, lymphoma, Merkel cell and palliative lesions, so its 84.9% two-year control is not a clean BCC/cSCC figure and probably understates what selected nonmelanoma disease would achieve. Pretibial skin is the one anatomic site where practice converges on gentler fractionation, after respondents reported non-healing ulcers.

What would make this body of evidence wrong? Longer follow-up revealing late failures or late fibrosis in the hypofractionated schedules, or a randomised comparison showing that surgical control advantages persist in the H-zone population these series target. Until then, the defensible read is that mould and flap HDR is a reasonable radiation option for superficial facial and ear lesions in pts who are poor surgical candidates, with depth assessment as the gate, and that the choice among the published schedules is less consequential than getting the target depth right. The absence of agreed dosimetric constraints, noted directly by the survey, means outcomes in less experienced hands may not match these reports.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Mould and flap HDR fits curved H-zone and pinna targets where electron or kV fields struggle, with prescription at 5 mm and margins near 5 mm. Hypofractionated twice-weekly 40 Gy/8 fx and daily 40 Gy/10 fx both carry acceptable toxicity; pretibial skin warrants 2-3 Gy per fraction per survey practice.
